components.input_conditions: A candidate sphere in residual Euclidean space U with dim U>=2 before a required cut, and 0<eta<1.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: One cut multiplies sinh S by sigma; at most one cut per query. Reuses P103 geometry, with the new primary budget calibration.
components.preserved_model_properties: Surviving physical minimizers do not move and remain on dist(o,p)=R. The common projection gives D=arcosh(cosh S cosh dist(c,z)), u_{z,p}=u_V+v/a, a=sinh D/sinh S, ||u_V||^2=1-a^-2.
components.transcript_control: One cut enlarges W by one residual direction and makes q public. Zero-cut and cached queries do not reduce the residual sphere.
components.transformation: Retain <e,v>=-eta; substitute v=-eta e+sigma w to obtain the exact center/radius update in the Oracle routine. Before every possible cut through horizon T, residual dimension is at least d-t>=2, so the latitude is nonempty. The new center is future-pointing unit timelike since the update numerator has Lorentz square -(1+sigma^2 sinh^2 S) and negative inner product with the old future-pointing center.

components.input_conditions: P compact convex in V and containing its current intrinsic public ball; contact data from Lemma6.5; 0<mu<=1/16.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: r_S=arsinh(eta tanh S); scalar persistence pays for future public-domain growth without an extra objective call.
components.preserved_model_properties: The Lorentz halfspace <n_p,x>_L<=0 contains old P, contains p strictly and has z on its boundary. For later representation p=cosh S'c'+sinh S'v', with S'<=S and W' containing old z,q, let a'=sinh D/sinh S'. Its projected normal n_W'=q+mu(cosh S'c'-cosh D z)/sinh D has square A_theta-mu^2/a'^2>0, and -<n_W',c'>_L=B_theta(a')tanh S'. Lemma6.1 then gives containment of closed B_{V'}(c',r_{S'}).
components.transcript_control: D,theta and physical normal stay unchanged for every surviving p. The same certificate contains every future inserted public ball even though those balls need not be nested.
components.transformation: Set tau=2mu/(1+mu^2), kappa=(1-mu^2)/(1+mu^2), a0=1/kappa and n_V=q_V+mu u_V. Lemma6.4 gives -a<n_V,u_V>>=eta||n_V||. For retained candidates n_p=q+mu u_{z,p}, theta=-<q,u_{z,p}> is common and mu<theta<=1. Define A_theta=1+mu^2-2mu theta, B_theta(a)=(theta-mu)a+mu/a and F_theta(a)=B_theta(a)/sqrt(A_theta-mu^2/a^2). Proposition6.6 gives F_theta(a')>=eta for all a'>=a, not just current a. For a>=a0 this follows from the scalar right-branch lemma; if a<a0 the public normal vanishes and theta>=tau; beta=0 is treated separately with nonzero public normal and no cut.

components.input_conditions: The full archived normal certificates and P equal to the convex hull of all installed public balls.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: Multiplication by L scales values/vectors and the floor, without adding calls. Compactness follows from the finite-dimensional compact convex hull of bounded sets.
components.preserved_model_properties: f=L F_{K,p} is globally geodesically convex, globally L-Lipschitz, has unique minimizer p with min f=0, and realizes every archived value and full selected global subgradient simultaneously after every finite prefix. Lemma5.4 uses D_i>0, unit q_i and n_i,p=q_i+mu u_{z_i,p} in N_K(z_i) to give F(y_i)=mu D_i+ell_i and -log_{y_i}z_i/ell_i in partial F(y_i), or q_i in partial F(z_i) when ell_i=0.
components.transcript_control: For an exterior historical query, <n_i,p,y_i>_L=sinh ell_i(1-mu theta_i)>0 while the normal is nonpositive on K. Thus a query stays outside the carrier even after its direction becomes public. Cached responses are consistent, and a fixed selection can be completed at every unqueried point.
components.transformation: Proposition7.1 inducts over new, cached and zero-cut queries. Every old normal contains old P and each newly installed ball, hence their closed convex hull. For each surviving p, K=closed gconv(P union {p}) is compact convex and every n_i,p is in N_K(z_i). Apply Lemma5.4 at every archived contact to the same K,p and use Lemma5.3 for the global objective.

components.input_conditions: The full state/archive invariants, deterministic algorithm and the stated T,d,epsilon.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: Hard dimension d=T+2; total cut count at most T; normalized floor gives gap >=2epsilon R, scaled floor >=2epsilon LR.
components.preserved_model_properties: The completion is one global function with one fixed selected subgradient map for the entire replayed run; all minimizers lie at radius R. Failure is objective error or failure to meet the budget-and-output promise on a legal fixed instance.
components.transcript_control: Induction on queries reproduces all simulated exact replies, the same output or the same decision to continue/stall. No adaptation to an algorithm's private random seed is justified.
components.transformation: Use eta^2<=65epsilon^2, -log sigma<=eta^2 and log(2cosh(R/2))>=zeta_R/4 to get T+1>zeta_R/(260epsilon^2). Choose p opposite the residual projection of the final output, or any surviving p at a budget-failure prefix, and fix the carrier and Oracle. Replay the deterministic algorithm against those fixed objects.

construction.definition: Use the hyperboloid H^d={x:<x,x>_L=-1,x0>0}, <x,y>_L=-x0y0+sum x_jy_j. State is W_t, V_t=H^d intersect W_t, c_t in V_t, residual radius S_t>0 and compact convex public domain P_t subset V_t. Initialize W0=span{o}, V0=P0={o}, c0=o, S0=R. Candidate minimizers are C_t={cosh S_t c_t+sinh S_t v: v in W_t perpendicular_L, ||v||=1}; candidates remain physical points on the original sphere dist(o,p)=R. Define r_S=arsinh(eta tanh S). P_t is the closed geodesic convex hull of every intrinsic public ball installed so far, including the current closed B_{V_t}(c_t,r_{S_t}). Maintain an archive of distinct queries, exact replies and contacts (z_i,q_i,D_i,theta_i). For a terminal surviving p set K_{t,p}=closed gconv(P_t union {p}) and f_{t,p}(y)=L min_{x in K_{t,p}}{mu dist(x,p)+dist(y,x)}. The query/update routine and full archive certificate are specified below.
construction.hidden_objects: The final surviving physical minimizer p and resulting fixed carrier/objective. During the public simulation no particular p is fixed; completion is chosen after the output or at a failing budget/nonreturn prefix, then deterministic replay establishes one fixed legal instance.
construction.parameters: R,L>0; 0<epsilon<=1/64; mu=4epsilon<=1/16; eta=2mu/(1-mu^2); sigma=sqrt(1-eta^2); T=floor(log(2cosh(R/2))/(-log sigma)); d=T+2. Public-ball and residual-sphere radii are different objects.
construction.public_information: Known o,d,R,L,epsilon and geometry; all simulated responses depend only on current public state and query. This mathematical simulation does not grant an optimization algorithm direct access to the hidden p or an extra carrier Oracle.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Limitation of the established argument, not a claim that randomization succeeds.
escape_conditions.statement: Randomized algorithms are outside the deterministic replay quantifiers; a seed-dependent final instance does not prove a randomized minimax bound.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Additional transfer obligations, not proved escape algorithms.
escape_conditions.statement: No transfer is established to noisy, stochastic, higher-order or specially structured supporting Oracles, or to smooth/strongly convex subclasses.
The hard dimension grows with T. A matching lower bound at a prescribed fixed dimension does not follow.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: The current proof requires the full archive; this does not assert impossibility of a different proof.
escape_conditions.statement: Dropping the convex hull of historical public balls or checking supports only at queried points removes the stated global completion certificate.

hardness_claims.algorithm_coverage: All deterministic adaptive algorithms with arbitrary ambient queries, arbitrary computation and arbitrary outputs, including unqueried outputs; no span or historical-halfspace restriction.
hardness_claims.missing_lifting: No randomized-algorithm, noisy-Oracle, fixed-d matching, smoothness or higher-order extension is established.
hardness_claims.regime_note: 0<epsilon<=1/64; R,L>0; d=T+2 and T as above. Every algorithm guaranteed to return within T calls has a single fixed legal witness with output gap >=2epsilon LR; budget excess and nonreturn have fixed-prefix witnesses. This yields the dimension-uniform lower constant 1/260.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: Every compact contact minimization has a solution; settle ties deterministically by successive coordinate minimization. Select on-domain e deterministically from a fixed ambient basis. For beta>0 retain <e,v>=-eta, write v=-eta e+sigma w, and set W_{t+1}=W_t direct-sum span{e}, sinh S_{t+1}=sigma sinh S_t, cosh S_{t+1}c_{t+1}=cosh S_t c_t-eta sinh S_t e, V_{t+1}=H^d intersect W_{t+1}, P_{t+1}=closed gconv(P_t union closed B_{V_{t+1}}(c_{t+1},r_{S_{t+1}})). If beta=0 make no cut and retain every candidate. Each distinct-contact response is independent of the final candidate choice. At completion assign cached selected subgradients at queried points and the unique minimum-norm subgradient elsewhere; Lemma5.2 ensures this defines a fixed map for f.
oracle_realizations.cost: One call returns a paired exact value/full tangent subgradient. Arbitrary internal computation, contact minimization and exact geometry are outside objective-call accounting. No efficient numerical implementation claim.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: Each actual cut reveals at most one residual direction while preserving an entire latitude of possible physical minimizers. Values and full vectors are exact, so small hidden components are never discarded. The archive certificate ensures all remaining candidates admit the entire exact transcript simultaneously; it is not a scalar-bit-information estimate.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: With k_t<=t actual cuts, sinh S_t=sigma^{k_t}sinh R, so S_t>=R/2 for t<=T. For arbitrary output xhat choose a unit residual v with <v,xhat>_L<=0 and p=cosh S_t c_t+sinh S_t v. Then cosh dist(xhat,p)>=cosh S_t cosh dist(xhat,c_t)>=cosh S_t, hence f_{t,p}(xhat)>=Lmu S_t>=2epsilon LR, while min f=0. Every queried value also is at least 2epsilon LR. If call T+1 is requested, fix a completion at prefix T to witness budget failure; if the algorithm stalls at a finite prefix, that prefix completion witnesses nonreturn.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: Accept any y in H^d. If repeated, return its cached pair with no state change. For a new y outside P_t choose z minimizing mu arcosh(cosh S_t cosh dist(c_t,x))+dist(y,x) over x in P_t; let ell=dist(y,z)>0 and q=log_z y/ell. For a new y in P_t set z=y, ell=0; with D=arcosh(cosh S_t cosh dist(c_t,z)), u_V=(cosh S_t c_t-cosh D z)/sinh D, choose any deterministic unit e in U=W_t perpendicular_L and set q_V=-mu u_V, beta=sqrt(1-mu^2||u_V||^2), q=q_V+beta e. In the exterior case decompose q=q_V+beta e with q_V in T_z V_t, beta=||q-q_V||>=0, e residual unit when beta>0, and use the same D. If beta>0 perform the latitude/update below; otherwise do not change the state. Return L(mu D+ell) and L(-log_y z/ell) when ell>0, or Lq when ell=0. Cache these and archive z,q,D and theta=-<q,u_{z,p}>, common to retained candidates.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: No sampling, noise or random hidden-seed distribution. Repeated queries return exactly the cached value and vector. Adaptive public simulation is converted to one fixed objective/selection by deterministic replay; it is not a randomized lower-bound argument.
